title: Refusing Meat
note: He defines this as giving up eating flesh. Eating flesh keeps killing going and also comes from it, so it is both cause and result of that sin. It can’t go with compassion, so this chapter follows that one.

couplets.plain: How can someone who eats other flesh to swell their own hold to compassion?
couplets.pm: Someone who eats the body of another creature to fatten their own: how can they practise compassion? They can’t. To think that useless fattening is of use, and to do this cruelty for it, makes them a cruel fool.

links.quote: eats other flesh to swell their own
links.reason: Fattening your own flesh on another’s rules out any claim to compassion.

couplets.plain: Those who don’t guard wealth don’t get to hold it. In the same way, those who eat flesh don’t get to hold compassion.
couplets.pm: Those who don’t guard wealth get no use from it. In the same way, those who eat flesh get no use from compassion. He rejects the view that people who eat flesh but mean no harm to any creature can still practise compassion.

links.quote: those who eat flesh don’t get to hold compassion
links.reason: As the careless cannot keep wealth, the eater of flesh cannot keep compassion.

couplets.plain: Like the heart of someone holding a weapon, the mind of one who has tasted a creature’s body doesn’t turn to good.
couplets.pm: The mind of someone holding a weapon looks only to the killing it can do, not to compassion. The mind of someone who eats another creature’s body for its taste, made sweet with spices, looks only to that flesh, not to compassion. So such a mind thinks of harm.

links.quote: the mind of one who has tasted a creature’s body doesn’t turn to good
the heart of someone holding a weapon
links.reason: Someone gripping a weapon is the comparison for a heart closed to good.

couplets.plain: What is compassion? Not killing. What is not? Killing. Eating that flesh is worthless.
couplets.pm: What is compassion? Not killing. What is not compassion? Killing. So eating the flesh that comes of killing is sin. Not compassion means cruelty. Some take it otherwise: what isn’t compassion is breaking the vow of not killing.
couplets.note: He takes பொருள் as righteousness, the thing of true worth, so “worthless” here means sin.

links.quote: What is compassion? Not killing. What is not? Killing
links.reason: Killing is named as the very opposite of compassion.

couplets.plain: Life endures in not eating flesh. Eat it, and hell won’t open its mouth to let you out.
couplets.pm: Some creatures stay alive in their bodies because of the righteousness of not eating flesh. If you eat it, the hell that swallowed you won’t open its mouth to spit you out, and you sink there for ages. He rejects the view that the sin of killing rests on the killer, so that the eater has none.
couplets.note: “To let you out” is his explanation. The Tamil says only that hell won’t open its mouth.

links.quote: Life endures in not eating flesh

couplets.plain: If the world didn’t kill in order to eat, no one would offer flesh for money.
couplets.pm: If the world’s creatures didn’t kill for the sake of eating, out of folly, no one would sell flesh for money. He answers those who say that eating comes after the killing, so it can’t cause it and the eater has no sin. Eating is a cause of the killing.

links.quote: no one would offer flesh for money
If the world didn’t kill in order to eat

couplets.plain: Flesh is another creature’s wound. If you know that, you must not eat it.
couplets.pm: Flesh is the wound of another body. If there are people who know it to be unclean, they must not eat it. People eat it only because they don’t know this truth. Reason too shows that eating flesh is low.

links.reason: Knowing flesh for a wound is enough to end the wish to eat it.

links.quote: If you know that, you must not eat it
links.reason: Asks the doubtful eater to see flesh as another creature’s wound and then decide.

couplets.plain: Those whose sight has parted from fault won’t eat flesh that has parted from life.
couplets.pm: Those whose understanding is free of the fault of delusion won’t eat flesh parted from a life. They know for themselves the truth that flesh is a corpse.

links.quote: won’t eat flesh that has parted from life
links.reason: Freedom from fault shows itself in refusing flesh parted from life.

couplets.plain: Better than pouring offerings into a thousand sacrifices is not to take one creature’s life and eat it.
couplets.pm: Better than a thousand sacrifices, with ghee and other offerings poured on the fire, is not to take the life of one animal and eat the flesh it lived in. The fruit of this vow is greater than the fruit of those sacrifices.

links.quote: not to take one creature’s life and eat it
Better than pouring offerings into a thousand sacrifices is not to take one creature’s life

couplets.plain: All living beings join their hands and worship one who doesn’t kill and refuses flesh.
couplets.pm: All living beings join their hands and worship someone who kills nothing and eats no flesh. Killing is named too, because one of these righteous acts is of no use without the other. Someone with such great compassion will rank above the gods in the next life.

links.quote: join their hands and worship one who doesn’t kill and refuses flesh
links.reason: All living beings join hands in reverence to one who refuses flesh.

ideaLinks.quote: those who eat flesh don’t get to hold compassion
ideaLinks.reason: Compassion cannot be held by one who eats flesh, any more than wealth by one who doesn’t guard it.
